prompt: A PR changes 4,000 lines across 60 files. Reviewers approve it after skimming because it's too big to read.
why: Huge changes don't get real review; split them.
trap: Testing matters too, but size is what broke the review.

prompt: An engineer splits a feature into three PRs: first a pure refactor, then the new API, then the UI that uses it.
tells: splits a feature into three PRs
why: Small, focused PRs are easier to review and undo.
trap: There's a refactor, but the move is how the work is sliced.

prompt: A one-line bug fix also reformats the whole file, so reviewers can't find the actual change.
why: Keep each change to one purpose.
trap: Cleanup can be good, but not mixed into a fix.

prompt: When a bug shows up, the team reverts one small commit and keeps the other eleven, because each did only one thing.
tells: because each did only one thing
why: Small commits make problems easy to isolate and undo.
trap: There's a revert, but the lesson is the commit size.

prompt: In a behavioral interview, a candidate says reviewers sped up once they started sending PRs under 200 lines.
why: Small PRs get faster, better reviews.
trap: Reviewers benefit, but the habit is the size of the change.

prompt: A branch has lived for six weeks and now conflicts with everything. The lead asks for work to be merged to main in daily slices instead.
tells: merged to main in daily slices
why: Small, frequent merges avoid painful big ones.
trap: Hiding unfinished work may need a flag, but the ask is slicing the work.
